requirements.requirement: On node1, restrict cron scheduling to only root and opsadmin users
requirements.summary: /etc/cron.allow created containing exactly 'root' and 'opsadmin' (mode 644, root:root). opsadmin was created since it did not previously exist. Verified root and opsadmin can use crontab (rc=0) while a throwaway crontestuser is rejected with 'not allowed to use this program' (cron.allow enforcement). Test crontab entries and the test user were cleaned up afterward.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1 with persisted cron access control after recovery
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured (boot_id 0d6209e2..., crond active, cron.allow=root/opsadmin). Reboot acknowledged via backgrounded shutdown -r now (rc=0). Node observed unreachable across two consecutive SSH timeouts, then reachable again. Post-restart boot_id (ece1d32b...) differs from baseline, confirming an actual reboot. Post-restart state shows crond active, cron.allow unchanged, opsadmin able to schedule a cron job, and a newly created test user denied. Cross-checked against fixed global before/after-executor boot-identity snapshots, which show the same boot_id transition and no failed services after recovery.

overall_summary: The executor satisfied the public task by restricting cron scheduling on node1 to root and opsadmin via /etc/cron.allow, with clear before/after enforcement checks (allowed users succeed, a disallowed test user is rejected). The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was also completed with direct evidence of a healthy pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, unreachability during reboot, a changed boot identity post-restart, and confirmed persistence and enforcement of the cron.allow policy after recovery. Hygiene is good: test artifacts were cleaned up, with only a trivial reboot.log file left behind as an expected byproduct of the restart mechanism.
limitations: Package-health checks were unavailable (timed out) both before and after, so full package-state integrity could not be independently confirmed.
No negative test was performed for a pre-existing non-privileged user (only newly created test users were checked), though this is a reasonable and sufficient proxy for cron.allow enforcement.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map clearly to the task or the restart-evidence protocol. Test users (crontestuser, crontestuser2) and their crontab entries were created for verification and subsequently removed via crontab -r / userdel -r (cmd-f374c927ea3b463f, cmd-fdbae127201d44c3), leaving no residue. The failed useradd attempt (cmd-c981f2c545f24a87, command not found) was a read-only-effect discovery error, not a mutation, and was corrected by using the full path via sudo. One minor residue: /tmp/reboot.log, created as the redirect target of the backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' command, remains present in the after-executor temporary-files snapshot; this is a low-risk, expected byproduct of the mandated reboot acknowledgement mechanism rather than an unnecessary mutation, but it was not cleaned up.
